verify.note: Each hook against the original from one state: every register with R and all memory (the bitmap too) at the draw hook, the erase-only entry, the clear, the pace window's entries and ends and every draw from its entry; the object's sprites against a model of the figure, and the model against the original's own plot wherever the entry draws without erasing; the colour paint's copies store nothing and leave everything else the game's; the IM 1 handler of the alt ROM image against Sinclair's at every interrupt; unit cases over every type.

status.title: Tranz Am
status.build: tranz_am_sprites.nex 91a66955 (the game draws as it does; the cars and the roadside items as sprites on the same pixels in their own colours; their colour paint stores nothing; loading screen)
status.software: Verify IDENTICAL on two whole machine-played recordings (40,164 frames, 14 games): 26,818 figures as sprites, 2,796,472 sprite pixels against the figure's model (itself checked against the original's plot at every draw-only entry), every register with R and all memory (the bitmap too) at every hook, the IM 1 handler compared at 39,986 interrupts; unit PASS (3,264 graphic cases over all 34 types, negative control 40 of 40); 6 of 6 broken builds detected; ROM path check pass
status.next: a recording played by hand; hardware test

techniques.target: the game's plotter and bitmap unchanged; each object's sprites lie on the pixels it plots, in the object's colour; the colour paint's two CALLs for objects go to a copy that stores nothing
HLIB_R_IN / hlib_r_set / HLIB_R_OUT in every hook (the game reads R)
HLIB_SPEED_IN at the plot's entries, HLIB_SPEED_OUT at their ends: the set-up runs at 28 MHz and pays for the draw hook
Sinclair's ROM as the alt image with the hooks at 0x386E (0xFF there); the game runs the ROM's IM 1 handler, compared at every interrupt

pacing.coverage: Two machine-played recordings (40,162 frames); every pace site compared in the replay. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: The main loop is not frame-synced. The plot's set-up, a fixed stretch a draw, runs at 28 MHz and pays for the draw hook (as Jetpac 1.3); the colour paint's copy takes the original's time to the T state. Not measured as a whole.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen writer of the first recording (survey); every CALL and JP from the handlers into the plot code listed; the colour paint's three callers checked by the build; all 34 types through the plotter in the unit cases.
dependencies.result: The bitmap and all game memory but the colour cells of the objects with sprites stay the original's. The game runs the ROM's IM 1 handler: the alt ROM image is Sinclair's. It reads R: every hook leaves R as the original. Two routines CALL the plot's set-up past its start with a place and a graphic of their own: those draws change no sprite (an entry marks an object's draw). A 16K game: nothing reads or writes above 0x7FFF, where the hook RAM is.

feasibility.decision: As Jetpac's published patch (owner 2026-11-20: 'Let's finish off the ultimate games'): the game's own colours, moving figures as sprites.
feasibility.next_experiment: A recording played by hand into later levels; hardware: the checklist in games/tranz_am.md; the game's speed against the original over a minute of play: within 2%.
